# Government Stimulus Packages You Should Keep an Eye out For


[wagetap](https://medium.com/@wagetap?source=post_page---byline--9ccf12693d3a---------------------------------------)


3 min read


·


May 7, 2020


--


With the[coronavirus in full swing worldwide](https://www.who.int/emergencies/diseases/novel-coronavirus-2019) , Australia has been[less affected by coronavirus than many other countries](https://edition.cnn.com/2020/05/01/asia/australia-coronavirus-success-intl-hnk/index.html) . But this has come at a price; economic movement has slowed and individuals and businesses alike have had to take on financial burdens. The Australian government has introduced[stimulus packages](https://www.smallbusiness.wa.gov.au/blog/coronavirus-stimulus-package-small-business) to support the economy to a total of $320 billion (and counting!). These are earmarked to support individuals, self-employed, and businesses. We’ve broken them down to help you better understand your eligibility for government support.


## For Individuals


The JobKeeper payment helps businesses significantly impacted by the coronavirus cover parts of their wage bill in order to avoid layoffs. Businesses can apply for fortnightly payment of $1500 on the employee’s behalf. To be eligible, the employee has to fill out a nomination form to meet eligibility and agree to the claim from the employer. The employer can still pay additional wages and make superannuation contributions. Find out more about JobKeeper payment[here](https://treasury.gov.au/sites/default/files/2020-04/Fact_sheet__JobKeeper_Info_for_Employees.pdf) .


If you are[eligible for the JobSeeker payment](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/individuals/services/centrelink/economic-support-payment/who-can-get-it) , the government will also be upping their support through the[Economic Support Payment](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/individuals/services/centrelink/economic-support-payment/how-much-you-can-get) , which will be disbursed along with your original payment. This will be released in two one-off payments.


In the case that you have been financially affected by COVID-19, you may be able to access some of your superannuation early. If you are an[eligible citizen or permanent resident](https://www.ato.gov.au/Individuals/Super/In-detail/Withdrawing-and-using-your-super/COVID-19-early-release-of-super/?page=1#Eligibility) , you can apply for up to $10,000 in both 2019–20 and 2020–21; if you are an eligible temporary resident, you can apply for up to $10,000 in 2019–20. These payments will be tax-free and you will not need to include it in your tax returns. Submit your[application online](https://www.google.com/search?q=mygov+australia&oq=mygov+au&aqs=chrome.1.69i57j0l5j69i60l2.2776j0j7&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8) before 30 June for the 2019–20 year and between 1 July and 24 September for the 2020–21 year.

## For the Self-Employed


If you are a sole trader, the government has temporarily expanded the JobSeeker eligibility criteria, allowing you to[access up to $1060 per fortnight depending on your circumstance](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/individuals/services/centrelink/jobseeker-payment/how-much-you-can-get) and an additional[$550 coronavirus supplement](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/individuals/services/centrelink/coronavirus-supplement) for the next 6 months. To apply, you have to meet the eligibility of a JobSeeker and have your application approved[website for Services Australia.](https://www.servicesaustralia.gov.au/)


Sole traders are also granted early special access to withdraw funds from superannuation. Withdrawals are capped at $10,000 for this year and next year, and will be completely tax-free. To apply,[visit this portal](https://my.gov.au/LoginServices/main/login?execution=e1s1) . This scheme is managed by the Australian Taxation Office (ATO), who will communicate the procedure to eligible applicants.


## For Businesses


Not-for-profits and small businesses with a turnover under $50 million are eligible to receive between $20,000 and up to $100,000 in cash to help keep business running and retain staff. These payments will be tax-free, and would be managed by the ATO. To understand how to apply and the necessary criteria to be eligible, visit the[ATO website](https://www.ato.gov.au/Business/Business-activity-statements-(BAS)/In-detail/Boosting-cash-flow-for-employers/?page=1) .


The government has also launched the[Small and Medium Enterprise (SME) Guarantee Scheme](https://treasury.gov.au/coronavirus/sme-guarantee-scheme) that aims to commit up to $40 billion to eligible SMEs, sole traders, and not-for-profits. The scheme guarantees 50 percent of new loans issued by participating lenders to SMEs, securing lenders’ willingness and ability to provide credit. This guarantee allows SMEs more access to much-needed funding during these difficult times. To participate, apply through the list of[participating lenders](https://treasury.gov.au/economic-response-coronavirus-coronavirus-sme-guarantee-scheme/list-participating-lenders) .


The government has included countless other relief programs that are specific for different individuals and businesses, whether it be through[tax](https://www.ato.gov.au/General/COVID-19/?=redirected_URL) ,[loan deferrals](https://www.smallbusiness.wa.gov.au/blog/new-banking-relief-announcement) , or[increased leniency](https://www.afsa.gov.au/about-us/newsroom/practitioners-covid-19-and-updated-advice-inspector-general) . To better understand what programs best work for your current situation, we suggest checking the[treasury website](https://treasury.gov.au/coronavirus) and the[ATO](https://www.ato.gov.au/) for more information.
